business_summary.text: Swiggy operates food delivery and quick commerce platforms in India, with Instamart being its quick commerce arm and Swiggy its food delivery platform.

call_points.text: Quick commerce contribution breakeven guided for the current quarter, for the full quarter.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated the breakeven target in memory, now dated to the current quarter

call_points.text: Capex of about ₹195 Cr went largely into warehousing; capex expected to come down from the last couple of years.
Quick commerce overheads run at about ₹700 Cr a quarter, a large part of it marketing spend.
About half the NOV-to-GOV gain came from stopping the No Fee experiment in the third week of January.
MTU growth faces headwinds from churning low-AOV, low-frequency users; management expects churn for another two quarters.
Non-grocery share in quick commerce is near 30%, expected to stay in the 30%-40% range.
Top city operates at 3% positive contribution margin and breaks even at EBITDA at city level.
Management declined to say when EBITDA profitability comes, calling it a choice to be made later.
Management would not guide on gross versus net MTU additions or forward MTU assumptions.
Toing is a separate app at a pre-PMF stage, not part of the core food delivery financials.
SNACC operations were shut down this quarter; a large part of the platform innovation cost relates to that closure.

guidance.statement: We remain on track for contribution margin breakeven in line with our guidance.

guidance.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin breakeven for the full quarter in the current quarter.
Quick commerce NOV ambition of ₹1 lakh Cr in 3.5 to 5 years at 35%-50% CAGR.
Food delivery medium-term growth of 18%-20% with steady-state EBITDA margin of 5%.

status_history.evidence: Food delivery GOV grew 17.7% YoY in Q2FY27; management confident of 18-20% full-year guidance ex-Toing.
Food delivery Adjusted EBITDA margin at 3.4% of GOV, +58 bps YoY, on path to 5% steady state.
Quick-commerce segment result widened to -₹764 Cr in Q2FY27 from -₹651 Cr in Q1FY27, against a guided contribution margin of 0 to -100 bps.
QC contribution margin at -1.0% of GOV, within the guided zero to -100 bps range.

operating_notes.text: Active dark stores reached 1,143 across 129 cities as of Q4FY26.
Food delivery GOV ₹9,005 Cr in Q4FY26 with adjusted EBITDA margin of 3.3% of GOV, a lifetime high.
Instamart operated 1,143 darkstores across 129 cities covering 4.8 million sq ft at Q4FY26, with average order value of ₹700.
Instamart monthly contribution margin reached -1.1% in March 2026 against a -1.8% quarterly figure.
Quick commerce overheads run at about ₹700 Cr a quarter, which management said would translate into ₹2,800 Cr of full-year EBITDA loss at that level.
Non-grocery share of quick commerce is near 30%, expected to stay in the 30%-40% range.
Store additions typically happen when a store hits 80%-85% capacity, with utilisation-based additions at around 80%-90%.
QC NOV growth at 10% in latest 4 weeks, up from 1% in previous 4 weeks
61% M1 retention of transacting users, highest in many quarters
Two-thirds of Toing users are new to Swiggy platform
Q2FY27 quick-commerce segment revenue ₹1,306 Cr with segment loss ₹764 Cr
Q2FY27 food delivery segment revenue ₹2,338 Cr with segment result ₹349 Cr
Lynks Logistics sold to Trustroot Internet for ₹500 Cr, deconsolidated September 15, 2026
Q2FY27 quick commerce added 69 net darkstores to 1,240 across 133 cities, with orders per darkstore per day at 1,192.
Q2FY27 food delivery take-rate reached a record 26.1%, up 23 bps YoY.
Lynks Logistics sold to Trustroot Internet (Udaan) for ~₹500 Cr; financials included through Q2FY27.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹6,383 Cr (+44.7% YoY), net loss ₹800 Cr (against a loss of ₹1,081.18 Cr a year earlier).
Swiggy released its Q4FY26 Shareholders' Letter highlighting robust revenue growth and improving unit economics.
Swiggy submitted the monitoring agency reports for IPO and QIP proceeds for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.
Swiggy Limited shared the audio recording of its Analysts and Investors Conference Call held on May 08, 2026, via its investor relations website.
Swiggy clarified its postal ballot notice regarding proposed amendments to support future Indian Owned and Controlled Company status.
Swiggy reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹6,383 Cr with a net loss of ₹800 Cr, highlighting progress towards quick commerce breakeven.
Swiggy announced postal ballot results where the AoA amendment resolution failed with 72.36% approval, while Renan De Castro Alves Pinto was appointed as Nominee Director.
Swiggy reports Q1FY27 earnings call transcript, outlining shift in QC strategy to growth with 0 to -100 bps CM flexibility while maintaining 18-20% food delivery growth guidance
Swiggy completed the sale of Lynks Logistics, terminating its status as a step-down subsidiary.
Swiggy approved the re-appointment of Anand Kripalu and Suparna Mitra as independent directors for second five-year terms.

Swiggy's Q2FY27 shareholder letter reported B2C GOV up 24.6% to ₹20,793 Cr, food delivery Adjusted EBITDA at a record ₹341 Cr, but consolidated Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹760 Cr on quick commerce burn.

Swiggy Limited made available the audio recording of the Conference Call for Analysts and Investors held on Thursday, October 22, 2026, via link https://www.swiggy.com/corporate/investor-relations/financial-results/
